title: self calls can resolve to another class in the same file
reasoning: The self branch chooses the first candidate in the caller's file without checking its owning class. When multiple classes define the same method, a call in one class can point to another class's method, making graph edges dependent on candidate ordering despite caller_qual_name being available.
reproduction: Pass candidates [(Path('m.py'), 'A.save'), (Path('m.py'), 'B.save')] for called_name='save', qualifier='self', caller_file=Path('m.py'), and caller_qual_name='B.run'. The result is m.py::A.save.
recommendation: Resolve self calls against the caller's class first and then its supported inheritance hierarchy; do not select unrelated same-file methods.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The supplied test does not cover call resolution or multiple classes sharing method names.
suggestedRegressionTest: Test same-named methods across classes and reorder candidate lists; resolution must remain tied to the caller's class.
minimumFixScope: The self-qualified branch of _resolve_call in graph.py.
